memory_update.text: Add ALAB, CRDO, MPWR, SNPS, CDNS, MU, DELL, ANET and INTC as additional US-listed research candidates for the AI accelerators/custom ASICs/compute platforms node.

The node should be tracked as a multi-layer chokepoint: accelerator silicon, custom ASIC design, foundry/advanced packaging, HBM, connectivity silicon/cables, EDA/IP, power delivery, and AI server integration.

Non-US-listed but important private/foreign comparables remain outside this 15-name list: SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, MediaTek, Alchip, Global Unichip, Socionext, Quanta, Wiwynn, Wistron, Foxconn, Lenovo, Huawei/Ascend, Cerebras, Groq, Tenstorrent and hyperscaler internal ASIC programs.

Need a separate Layer 1B pass for optical networking and CPO suppliers because COHR, LITE, CIEN, FN and other optics/connectivity names may be more directly mapped to the AI networking node than to accelerator/custom ASIC compute platforms.

Custom ASIC exposure should be treated as a beneficiary and a substitution risk: AVGO/MRVL/EDA/IP vendors can benefit as hyperscalers diversify, while merchant GPU leaders may still dominate if software and time-to-market advantages remain decisive.

node: AI accelerators, custom ASICs, and compute platforms
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI accelerator/custom ASIC/compute-platform node. The highest-confidence direct exposures remain NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Marvell, TSMC, Arm, Micron, and Astera Labs. Second-order but relevant exposures include EDA/IP vendors, accelerator power-delivery suppliers, AI server/platform integrators, and Ethernet AI-networking platforms. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list.
